MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: [redacted name]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (AD-HSP). Patient previously tested negative for sequence variants in SPAST and ATL-1 genes. Current testing requested to continue diagnostic investigation.

TEST PERFORMED
DNA sequencing analysis of ATL-1 (SPG3a), REEP1 (SPG31) and NIPA1 (SPG6) genes

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leucocytes. Prior MLPA analysis was performed using the SALSA MLPA probemix P165 HSP kit (MRC-Holland), which covers all exons of the spastin gene (SPAST) and 13 of the 14 coding exons of the atlastin gene (ATL-1). Current testing involved fluorescent DNA sequencing of the complete coding regions and intron-exon boundaries of ATL-1 (SPG3a), REEP1 (SPG31) and NIPA1 (SPG6) genes. The analytical sensitivity of this method is >98% for the detection of point mutations and small insertions/deletions (microlesions).

RESULTS

ATL-1 (SPG3a) gene (NM_015915.4):
Heterozygous variant detected: c.705C>T (p.Phe235Phe)
Classification: Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS)
This variant results in a synonymous change and is likely non-pathogenic.

REEP1 (SPG31) gene (NM_022912.2):
No pathogenic mutations detected

NIPA1 (SPG6) gene (NM_144599.5):
No pathogenic mutations detected

Previous testing:
SPAST (Spastin) gene: No pathogenic mutations detected (prior analysis)
ATL-1 gene: No pathogenic mutations detected in prior sequencing

INTERPRETATION
A heterozygous variant of uncertain significance was identified in the SPG3a/ATL-1 gene: c.705C>T (p.Phe235Phe). This variant results in a synonymous amino acid change (phenylalanine to phenylalanine at position 235) and is likely to be non-pathogenic. No other pathogenic mutations were detected in the ATL-1, REEP1, or NIPA1 genes.

The genetic diagnosis of AD-HSP has not been confirmed by this analysis. However, these results do not exclude a diagnosis of AD-HSP as mutations in other genes not tested here may be causative. Mutations in SPAST and SPG3a account for approximately 50% of AD-HSP cases, while REEP1 mutations account for approximately 7.5% of cases.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Presymptomatic testing for the c.705C>T variant detected in the ATL-1 gene is not recommended given its likely non-pathogenic nature.

Further genetic testing may be considered if clinically indicated, including:
- Extended HSP gene panel testing
- Whole exome sequencing
- Clinical reassessment and consideration of alternative diagnoses

This report has been reviewed and authorised by:
[redacted name], PhD, FRCPath
Consultant Clinical Scientist
